items.title: Petit Planet, aka HoYoverse's Take on Animal Crossing, Is Packed With Charm and Attention to Detail | IGN Preview
items.excerpt: 2026 has been an incredibly crowded year for cozy life simulation games. Ironically, a genre that people usually turn to when they need a break from intense action games has started to wear me out. After playing Animal Crossing: New Horizons' latest update, Starsand Island; Pokémon Pokopia; Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream; and more, I found myself suffering from a different kind of fatigue. The fact that Petit Planet still managed to hook me despite all that says a lot about how it’s shaping up.
items.content_text: Key Preview Takeaways: It will remind you a lot of Animal Crossing. This isn't a bad thing! There are some nice touches that go beyond Animal Crossing that I appreciate. The Switch 2 version won't be out until next year. 2026 has been an incredibly crowded year for cozy life simulation games. Ironically, a genre that people usually turn to when they need a break from intense action games has started to wear me out. After playing Animal Crossing: New Horizons' latest update, Starsand Island; Pokémon Pokopia; Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream; and more, I found myself suffering from a different kind of fatigue. The fact that Petit Planet still managed to hook me despite all that says a lot about how it’s shaping up. As this genre continues to evolve in different directions, Petit Planet, developed by HoYoverse, aka the company behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail, is a game that follows closely in the footsteps of Animal Crossing. In particular, its inspiration from Animal Crossing: New Horizons, which introduced outdoor furniture placement and crafting to the series, is immediately apparent. Petit Planet is built around the concept of living on your own uninhabited planet. After a simple character creation process, you sign up for a program offered by a company called Loomi Co., which lets you settle on an uninhabited planet. Guided by a dog named Mobai, you choose a planet with your preferred ecosystem and begin your new life. Mobai and his companions move in alongside you and help you get settled. Mobai essentially fills the same role as Tom Nook in Animal Crossing. Petit Planet even makes a direct reference to its inspiration when he hands you a temporary housing kit, asking something along the lines of, "Wait, they made you take out a loan on your previous planet?" He reassures you that there's no such system here, which sounds wonderful—until you discover that upgrading your temporary home to a proper house still costs money. Sure, there's no loan, but that's only because you have to pay upfront! Tom Nook's influence is alive and well in this one. The opening hours also feel remarkably similar to Animal Crossing. Shake a tree and fruit falls to the ground, with each planet having its own native fruit. You can decorate your tiny temporary home with furniture, change your character's clothes, catch bugs with a net, and fish with a rod. Fish and insects can be sold, used for cooking, or donated to a facility called the Eco House, which serves much the same purpose as the museum in Animal Crossing. Despite using New Horizons as a clear foundation, Petit Planet has some interesting features that make it feel distinct. Even the little details are familiar. Nearby animals applaud or compliment you when you successfully catch a bug or fish, and newly discovered creatures come with amusing descriptions. That said, despite using New Horizons as a clear foundation, Petit Planet has some interesting features that make it feel distinct. For example, in addition to fishing and bug catching, you can use a tong to collect shellfish and other creatures in shallow water. I particularly enjoyed trying to catch hermit crabs hiding beneath rocks, carefully timing my approach for the moment they emerged. The way your planet develops is also quite different from anything in Animal Crossing. At the center of your planet stands a tree named Luca, which initially resembles the Town Tree seen in earlier Animal Crossing games. By completing various activities, you earn opportunities to water it, causing the tree to grow. As the tree grows, the entire planet begins to change. At first, the changes are relatively small, such as flowers blooming nearby. Eventually, however, rivers and even oceans appear. Each stage of the tree's growth transforms the landscape, introducing new terrain and expanding the world around you. Growing this tree effectively serves as the game's main objective, giving you a reason to complete the various tasks scattered throughout your daily life. Animal Crossing meets dating sim? The arrival of new animal residents is another area where Petit Planet takes a familiar idea and develops it further. As you progress, more animals gradually visit your planet, but rather than simply moving in, their introductions play out as little story events. You need to complete their individual story missions before they agree to settle down. The objectives themselves can be quite simple, such as catching a particular insect for someone, but these quests effectively serve as character introductions, giving each resident a little more personality before they become part of your community. Once the animals have moved in, they'll continue asking you for favors. Interacting with them gradually increases a relationship meter, almost as though Animal Crossing had borrowed a few mechanics from a dating sim. Each character has their own specialties, likes, dislikes, and backstory. As your relationship grows, you learn more about them and receive rewards along the way. In that sense, Petit Planet gives you a clearer incentive to interact with your neighbors than Animal Crossing does, and seems determined to expand upon the idea of actually living alongside these characters. Of course, there's a potential downside to this approach. If the game isn't careful, living with your neighbors could start to feel less like a natural relationship and more like completing a checklist to maximize their affection. That's something I'd like to examine more closely after spending additional time with the game. The inclusion of voice acting is just one indication of how much effort HoYoverse has put into Petit Planet's presentation. Personally, what impressed me most was the attention to detail in its animations. For example, when your character stands up from a chair, they gently push it back into place with their hand. It might sound like an oddly specific thing to get excited about, but I can't recall seeing that animation in many other games. Likewise, when digging a hole with a shovel, your character places a foot on the top of the blade and presses down, just as someone would in real life. These small touches make everyday activities feel surprisingly convincing and help bring the planet to life. The gestures you gradually unlock as you progress are equally well-animated, making the photo mode particularly enjoyable. At one point, I was lying on the beach when I noticed another character running around in the shallow water nearby. Watching this little scene unfold made me appreciate just how lively and charming the world of Petit Planet can be. Furniture heaven There's no denying that Petit Planet shares so many similarities with Animal Crossing that some players may accuse it of being too derivative. A system called Loomix Footprints, which rewards small everyday accomplishments with a special currency, is strongly reminiscent of Nook Miles. Likewise, learning how to craft new items by reading Create Cards feels almost identical to collecting DIY recipes. And yet, Petit Planet remains immensely appealing. Part of that comes from the unique concept of living on a planet, but I suspect much of its appeal simply comes down to the exceptionally high quality of its execution. The furniture you can craft is consistently attractive, which only makes me want to spend more time decorating both my house and the surrounding landscape. I also had the opportunity to play a build with a considerable amount of progress already made. My character had access to a huge collection of furniture and clothing, allowing me to experiment freely with all sorts of decorative possibilities. Browsing through these items made me wonder whether Petit's greatest strength might actually be the sheer quantity and quality of its customization options. For someone like me, who spent countless hours decorating the interiors of houses and designing the landscape of my island in Animal Crossing, there's more than enough here to keep me occupied for a very long time. For someone like me, who spent countless hours decorating the interiors of houses and designing the landscape of my island in Animal Crossing, there's more than enough here to keep me occupied for a very long time. There are plenty of items that naturally belong outdoors, too. Alongside familiar objects such as vending machines, which are also available in Animal Crossing, you'll find things like bus stops. With such a wide variety of furniture, it's easy to imagine creating entire residential neighborhoods, shopping streets, parks, and other themed areas. Given the game's Chinese origins, I was also pleased to see a generous selection of East Asian-inspired furniture. I decided to turn a Chinese pond into a makeshift bathtub, transforming one of the rooms in my house into a Chinese style bathroom. Of course, not everyone enjoys designing an entire space from scratch. That's where the Blueprint system comes in handy. By placing the required furniture in designated positions, you can complete a predesigned facility or area. Better still, these creations aren't merely decorative. The residents of your planet actually make use of them. During my play session, I followed a Blueprint to set up a projector, a popcorn machine, chairs, and more on the beach. Once everything was in place, an event was triggered in which the residents gathered to watch a movie together. Seeing everyone happily enjoying a space I'd created gave me a sense of satisfaction that went beyond simply arranging furniture. This was actually one of the aspects of Animal Crossing that I had always found somewhat lacking. Throwing snowballs I also got to experience Petit Planet during the winter season. Here, my planet had been transformed into a snowy wonderland. Snow covered the rooftops and trees, giving the familiar scenery an entirely different atmosphere. What impressed me most was that even some of the larger pieces of furniture I'd placed outdoors were covered in snow. Seasonal changes are nothing new to Animal Crossing, of course, but seeing player-placed furniture change its appearance to match the season felt like a particularly nice touch. Petit Planet reportedly features more than 1,000 free furniture and clothing items in total. Just imagining the amount of work involved in creating seasonal variations for even a portion of those items is enough to make my head spin. Naturally, winter brings its own activities as well. Clearing away piles of snow rewards you with snowflakes, which can then be used to craft seasonal items such as the sled and a snowmonster. Eager to craft as many winter-themed decorations as possible, I started clearing snow wherever I could find it. To my surprise, one particular snow pile was hiding an incense burner underneath. Little discoveries like this help prevent what could otherwise be a repetitive chore from becoming monotonous. I was also surprised by the way you can throw snowballs. Rather than simply pressing a button to toss one, you can actually aim your throw using a targeting system reminiscent of a third-person shooter. Life simulation games tend to favor simple controls, but Petit Planet seems happy to borrow ideas from other genres. This approach makes its everyday activities feel more believable and interactive. And yes, you can also roll snowballs around to make them bigger, then stack two of them together to build a snowman. It seems that all the classic winter activities are accounted for. Too busy for a hot spring? Petit Planet also features seasonal events, and this time I got to experience one called the Season of Snowfall. takes place at a hot spring resort on another planet, where you meet the manager, Heyu, and help out with various tasks around the establishment. The gameplay mostly consists of straightforward errands, but the accompanying stories are so charming that I found myself eager to see what would happen next. My favorite encounter involved a tiny rabbit named Maxwell, who happens to be a movie director. Apparently, he'd come to the area to scout locations for his next movie. He made a point of insisting that he had absolutely no intention of taking a dip in the hot springs himself. Yet a little while later, he returned with his teeth chattering from the cold. After I guided him to the hot springs, he happily jumped into the water wearing a swim ring. Apparently, as thanks for saving him from freezing to death, he's going to include my name in the special thanks section of his movie's credits. Some players will undoubtedly feel that Petit Planet is simply too similar to Animal Crossing, and I can understand that criticism. However, it's worth remembering how Pokémon Pokopia borrowed numerous elements from Animal Crossing as well, while still managing to create an experience that felt fresh and distinctive. HoYoverse itself has been through something similar before. Prior to the release of Genshin Impact, that game faced criticism for its resemblance to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. Once it launched, however, it quickly became clear that Genshin Impact had plenty of its own ideas and offered a distinctive experience. I believe Petit Planet has every chance of following a similar path, drawing inspiration from Animal Crossing while developing an identity that players can appreciate on its own terms. In particular, its online features, which allow players to connect with one another, appear to be considerably more extensive than those in Animal Crossing. Unfortunately, I haven't had the chance to explore these systems thoroughly enough to offer a proper assessment just yet. I also had the opportunity to spend some time with the recently announced Nintendo Switch 2 version. As it was still a work-in-progress build, I noticed a bit of frame rate stuttering, and there were noticeable visual differences compared to the PC version. Given how well cozy life simulation games are suited to the Nintendo Switch 2, I'm hoping the developers will be able to further polish this version ahead of its planned release in 2027 after the PC and mobile versions drop on December 4. While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently! Stranger Than Heaven Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember Exodus Esra Krabbe is an editor at IGN Japan .

items.title: Nvidia Launches Investigation Into CEO Jensen Huang Following Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy
items.excerpt: Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
items.content_text: Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The tech giant's board confirmed the news in a statement today, saying that it is looking into its concerns "in light of recent reporting" that Huang has "been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The update follows a late-October New York Times report , which stated the CEO had been unfaithful to his wife with an individual that U.S. intelligence believed to be involved in a Chinese spy plot. The individual named in the report as having a relationship with Huang was Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. The CEO confirmed the affair in a letter sent to Nvidia staff (via BBC ). "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children,” he said. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation," he added. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. "I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American." Nvidia said that a committee of independent directors would oversee the effort with the assistance of outside independent counsel. The board said that it currently has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." The full statement follows: "The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. "Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate." Huang will remain Nvidia CEO as the investigation continues. The New York Times' report said that, as of last year, U.S. officials did not believe he was aware of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China. items.title: Why Austin Butler Cannot Drive the Iconic Black Ferrari in Miami Vice '85
items.excerpt: New videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan's Ricardo Tubbs driving a white Ferrari Testarossa, the wrong car for the period of the TV series that director Joseph Kosinski’s film is retelling. And there’s likely a legal reason for that.
items.content_text: New videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan's Ricardo Tubbs driving a white Ferrari Testarossa, the wrong car for the period of the TV series that director Joseph Kosinski’s film is retelling . And there’s likely a legal reason for that. In the first two seasons of the 1980s TV series , Don Johnson’s detective Sonny Crockett drove a black 1972 Ferrari Daytona Spyder convertible before it was blown up by a Stinger missile in the Season 3 premiere. (Cue the gaping Crockett meme.) In the show’s canon, Crockett’s cars were seized assets from criminals and loaned to him by the Miami-Dade Police Department as part of his undercover identity. The department supplied Crockett with a white 1986 Ferrari Testarossa in the second episode of Season 3. 🚨| Austin Butler and Michael B. Jordan back on the streets of Brooklyn filming ‘Miami Vice ‘85’ 🎬🌴 Sonny Crockett and Ricardo Tubbs, the city is yours 😎🔥 https://t.co/AWnbL6W400 — Miami Vice ‘85 Crave (@MiamiViceCrave) November 8, 2026 The Daytona Spyder seen on the show, however, was a replica built on a Corvette C3 chassis since Ferrari North America refused to provide the show with an authentic model. Ferrari launched a legal battle against the show and the replica builder, McBurnie Coachcraft, citing trademark infringement and brand dilution. “They eventually settled the dispute, winning broad legal protections for their trademarks and even the ‘shape and profile’ of the car,” recapped by @CinemaIsLife on X. “As a part of the settlement they donated two authentic Testarossas (their new flagship car) to the production—but only on the condition that the fake Daytona be dramatically blown up on national television.” It would appear then that Universal is simply avoiding another legal headache by jettisoning the Daytona Spyder from Miami Vice ‘85 and going with the white Testarossa even though it violates canon. Miami Vice ‘85 has been filming in New York and New Jersey but will shift production to Miami once hurricane season is over. The film opens in theaters, including IMAX, on May 19, 2028.

items.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says He 'Experiments With AI' Just to Make Sure It's Not 'Good at Writing' Yet
items.excerpt: Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad."
items.content_text: Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad." The Batman v. Superman and A Real Pain star explained why he finds the rapidly advancing and controversial technology unnerving – and how he deals with it – during a conversation with Variety . As he continues to plant his feet in Hollywood as a talent who can act, write, and direct, AI is something he's trying to keep his eye on in more ways than one. "I have a paranoid answer for this," Eisenberg said when asked if he's nervous about the technology. "I’m totally paranoid. I sometimes experiment with AI to see whether it's good at writing. And it's still not. "I’m paranoid, so I check and it still isn't. Thank God. I say, 'Write a scene like this.' I'm just testing it to make sure it's bad, and it's still bad. So I'm relieved, but, like, how far away is it from being good? How far are we from a kid putting on a pair of goggles and saying, 'I want to watch a movie about me where I rob a bank and then kiss the girl I’m in love with at school. Here are pictures of her, here are pictures of me' and then they press play? I'm paranoid about that." While figures like George Lucas have supported AI in the past, there are plenty of entertainers who have spoken out against the technology as it has advanced in recent years. Goku's voice actor in Dragon Ball, Masako Nozawa, blasted those who had used AI to steal her voice for their own use . Nicolas Cage said he'll "probably not work with" Amazon again after he declined to sign its AI waiver. Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto said Nintendo would prefer to "go in a different direction" when speaking about the topic in September. Eisenberg elaborated on his approach, saying that there are two saving graces: the power of the creative spirit and art that has stood the test of time. As AI development progresses to new and often intimidating places, these are the things that bring him some peace. "Creative spirit will find ways to entertain and delight us and speak about things in a way that maybe computers won’t," he added. "The other thing I think about all the time, and [The Debut star Julianne Moore is] about to go to a play in New York, is that I do these Greek plays, which were written 2,500 years ago and we perform them the same way they were performed 2,500 years ago. If they’ve lasted that long, they’ll still be there. "People want to be in the same room as other people, watching and listening to stories. It’s as old as cave people sitting by the campfire telling stories, and there will always be room for that. What I do worry about is whether we’ll still be able to make a living from it. I’m not 100% sure about that." Eisenberg's next movie is The Debut , which is set to arrive December 11, 2026. In related news, the moviemaker recently reflected on how winning a Razzie for his role as Lex Luthor affected his career . In June, he talked about what it was like to turn down an opportunity to return as Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network sequel . Photo by Zak Hussein/Variety via Getty Images.

items.title: Former PlayStation Boss Says Sony Doesn't Need a 'PS6 for $1,200,' It Needs a 'PS5 for $300'
items.excerpt: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he thinks innovation at Sony shouldn't come "from making a PS6 for $1,200" but from making "another PS5 for $300."
items.content_text: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he thinks innovation at Sony shouldn't come "from making a PS6 for $1,200" but from making "another PS5 for $300." As tech costs skyrocket and rumors of pricey gaming consoles swirl, the former president and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America took the time on The Trophy Room podcast to encourage the PlayStation maker to consider an unexpected, cheaper course of action. Pointing out how previous hardware leaps have typically offered clearly identifiable innovative qualities from generation to generation, he touched on why the PlayStation 6 simply leaning on "more ray tracing and more teraflops" might not be the best idea. As Layden put it, "I think we have enough power in the machine." "The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200. It's to make another PS5 for $300," he added. "Now, that would be true innovation. This is the first platform that I've seen that has gone up in price over time. I mean, PS2, at the end of the PS2 era, it was $99. You could buy a PS2 for $99." The PS5 launched almost exactly six years ago with two primary options for players to choose from: a base version with a disc drive for $499, and a Digital Edition for $399. What seemed like relatively fair price points in 2020 now seems almost like a steal thanks to a series of price increases in recent years. Today, buying a base PS5 directly from PlayStation costs $649, a Digital Edition costs $599, and a Pro costs an unbelievable $899 (up $200 from its reveal price ). Things get even worse when you look at retailers like GameStop . Sony has put the blame on "continued pressures in the global economic landscape ," but that's done little to lessen the sting for the average buyer. As console sales for Sony, Microsoft , and Nintendo suffer, Layden is of the mind that Sony shouldn't be looking for a way to get to a likely more expensive future but instead a cheaper past. "I think if I were in their shoes, that's what I'd be doing. I'd be trying to find a way to get the cost down on the 5," he added. Later, he continued: "It's a hard place to be right now, I think. What the company needs to do is do what it's never done, which is, don't iterate the console. Make it smaller, make it cheaper, do all the things you can around that, but the silicon's fine, the OS is fine. It's more than enough power to build the kind of games all of us want to play." If you look at the raw console release timeline, we're just about due for the next PlayStation, but many players say they don't want to see a PS6 announced until hardware prices come down. In May, Sony said it was still trying to decide when its next console should launch . It followed a February report that stated the company was considering pushing the device to 2028 – or even 2029 – following previous 2027 launch expectations. For now, however, we know distressingly little about the PS6. As PlayStation continues battling the backlash against its decision to kill physical discs , one leaker has said RAM and storage for the console alone could cost as much as $680 . Meanwhile, an October patent suggested Sony may be looking into taking advantage of its own take on frame generation . How much the PS6 will cost when all is said and done is a mystery, but the future isn't looking particularly bright .
items.title_en: Former PlayStation Boss Says Sony Doesn't Need a 'PS6 for $1,200,' It Needs a 'PS5 for $300'

items.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Stomps on Expectations With $63 Million Box Office Opening Weekend
items.excerpt: Godzilla Minus Zero crushed expectations with a strong $63 million in its opening weekend at the global box office.
items.content_text: Godzilla Minus Zero crushed expectations with a strong $63 million in its opening weekend at the global box office. Director Takashi Yamazaki's Minus One sequel performed in theaters with an estimated $31.6 million domestically and $31.4 million internationally. That's at least a few stories above distributor domestic projections, which had Godzilla propped up to open in the mid-to-low $20 million range (via The Hollywood Reporter ), securing its title as the biggest opening for a live-action foreign language film ever . "War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus," an official description said. "Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here." Where its predecessor focused on one lone pilot named Koichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki) who found himself caught in the middle of post-war Japan's first run-in with Godzilla, Godzilla Minus Zero turned the focus to a new, otherworldly threat: King Ghidorah . Toho has mostly done its best to keep the classic kaiju antagonist's design a secret in the lead-up to the sequel's release, so don't worry, we won't spoil anything here. Although images and even shoddy theater recordings have polluted the internet in the few days since the film's release, the Godzilla vs. Ghidorah rematch almost certainly played a part in encouraging audiences to buy a ticket early. Godzilla Minus Zero also pulled in $21.3 million in global IMAX returns alone, breaking the record for an opening for a Japanese IMAX film. Booming audio aside, Godzilla has been going strong for the last decade or so. While films like the brutal Godzilla Minus One and Shin Godzilla helped reclaim the King of the Monsters' crown as a theatrical force to be reckoned with, Legendary has also kept other audiences entertained with its take on the character. Included in a cinematic universe known as the Monsterverse, this version of Godzilla has appeared in everything from a 2014 standalone film to team-ups with King Kong. The most recent arrived with Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire in 2024, with another sequel, Godzilla x Kong: Supernova , due out in March of next year. Legendary's Monsterverse has benefited from solid box office returns, but Yamazaki's vision for Godzilla has earned the atomic lizard critical acclaim. More than three years removed from its 2023 release date, Godzilla Minus One still boasts a 99% from critics and 98% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes (IGN gave it an 8/10 ). It also famously won an Oscar for VFX at the 96th Academy Awards . Godzilla Minus Zero holds an admittedly lower 90% from critics and 96% from audiences on the review aggregating website . IGN's 7/10 review said the sequel "ups the ante on the carnage" but didn't quite manage to have the same impact with its human characters. "Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front," we said, "but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held." Time will tell if Godzilla Minus Zero is looked back upon as fondly as the film it follows. In the meantime, the kaiju and his three-headed archnemesis are enjoying their time as kings of the worldwide box office. Competition for the weekend included Ramayana: Rise of a Legend , which earned $55.7 million, and the new animated Dr. Seuss movie, The Cat in the Hat , which earned $30.5 million. Elsewhere at the box office, we had Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything , which continued to attract eyes with another $8.8 million for the weekend and $79.8 million total, domestically. DC Studios' Clayface 's domestic total is now at $56.6 million, with its global haul hardening at $109 million. Godzilla Minus Zero also stars Minami Hamabe as Noriko Oishi, Hidetaka Yoshioka as Kenji Noda, and Min Tanaka as Kanji Murakami. Despite the movie's promise of "no third time," Yamazaki recently said he's "fifty-fifty" on whether or not he'll return for another sequel . For a better idea of how the story could continue with Godzilla Plus One (or whatever it ends up being called), you can read IGN's spoiler-y breakdown of Godzilla Minus Zero's ending . You can also check out how we think the rest of Godzilla's rogues' gallery could be utilized , and then read about the household inspiration for the movie's final fight .

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Speedrunners Have Already Found New Ways to Break the Remake
items.excerpt: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake.
items.content_text: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake. One of the best things about a new Zelda game is seeing just how quickly players can speed through it, but Nintendo's latest video game being a remake presents a unique situation. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has accumulated some of the most bizarre speedrunning strategies in its 28 years on the market, and in just a few days, the Nintendo Switch 2 remake looks like it will live up to that legacy. Creative players started peeling back the layers of the new version of Link and Zelda's classic adventure just hours after it launched November 5. Even just moments into its life, they've discovered some seemingly useful (and hilarious) ways to break the game, with more almost certainly to be discovered in the weeks, months, and years ahead. Let's start with what might be the most common tactic under investigation so far: sending Link hurdling into the air at high speed. Ocarina of Time Remake speedrunning has begun https://t.co/lnEvgaHgj0 — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026 Ocarina of Time speedrunner Zfg1 seems to be one of the first to discover that the Switch 2 Zelda remake has interesting physics, which, if pushed far enough, can toss Link into the air like a firework. Even at first glance, you can probably guess how a safe landing from that height opens the door for players to get creative and skip portions of the game. It seems relatively easy to replicate, too, with X/Twitter user @Vespher also sharing footage of them pulling off the same stunt in the same location. Other locations seem to be susceptible to Link's sudden weightlessness with some careful positioning, with a similar area highlighted by other players . You might think that Link will only be able to fling himself skyward in extremely specific locations, but fear not, as there are other ways to send him for a ride. Another popular glitch making the rounds in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's first weekend in the public's hands only asks Hyrule's hero to stand in a chest. A few sudden movements (or even a well-placed bomb), and poof, ceiling. Nocturne skip with a normalized setup and a buffered ocarina actor jump (ez mode) https://t.co/QvtrVKYnC1 — Vespher (@Vespher) November 7, 2026 特定の宝箱の上でめっちゃ高く飛べるバグ ネタバレ注意 #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/y2Y5htiSTd — かえる (@k4erup) November 7, 2026 時のオカリナリメイク完全に理解した https://t.co/AoSYzB33ob — せーら姫 (@sera18171) November 7, 2026 Like so many other frequently speedrunned games out there, Ocarina of Time players have picked it apart to find the fastest means of traversal. Whether it's walking backward, hopping, or rolling, there are plenty of different ways to get around Hyrule. Nintendo has done its best to make speed concerns a thing of the past in the Switch 2 remake thanks to Link's new sprint feature. Did that stop fans from finding faster alternatives? Of course not. In fact, hilariously, early speedrunning strats show that rolling, again, may have emerged victorious as the ultimate way to get to the final fight against Ganondorf as quickly as possible. There are two seemingly faster options so far: one involving hopping, and one without. The former, as outlined by YouTuber KnightPohtaytoe , requires players to target-hop forward into a roll and seems marginally faster than sprinting. The latter, shown by Reddit user Pomps8a , is a bit easier to get the hang of and simply asks Link to cancel his roll with a quick attack. As this story is being written, the Zelda community has already found even more ways to skip sections of the game. One that started being shared around earlier today lets players climb walls by simply switching items. You can roll faster in ocarina by canceling with an attack by u/Pomps8a in NintendoSwitch2 デクの棒でジャンプ斬りする瞬間に他アイテムに切り替えることで高い足場にも届くバグが見つかった ほかの場所でも使えそう #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/DuDoGidQu7 — かえる (@k4erup) November 7, 2026 All the speedrunning stats are still coming in , but so far, it looks like it will take the average player about 20 hours or so to beat The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. Content creator @MrGymnast86 is one speedrunner who started gunning for the fastest time out of the gate and managed to complete an Any% run in a little less than four-and-a-half hours . It's a time that will almost surely shrink as more methods are developed by the community. The players looking to uncover sequence breaks – the ones who really want to get that game timer down just mere seconds if they can make it work – have found ways to allow Young Link to perform tasks only available to Adult Link and vice versa. As you might have guessed, the Ocarina of Time remake…doesn't really know how to tell the difference between the two if progress is made illegitimately. The results are almost impossible to describe, so you can see what some players have managed to capture below. Using a glitch to get a really big jump in the remake, its now possible to get the silver gauntlets chest as adult, which is supposed to be gotten as child. The cutscene that plays after tries to fit adult link into child link model, which ends up looking like this. https://t.co/un9DflnvxT — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026 This isn't possible with glitches yet, but if we can find a way to get into an adult only cutscene as child, we'll see this. https://t.co/0DC756ZLJV — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now for Switch 2. For more, you can see why IGN gave it a 9/10 review . You can also read about the developers who helped reimagine the Nintendo 64 classic for a modern audience. Image credit: @zfg111 on X/Twitter.

items.title: Epic Reveals Drop Rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token Following Pressure From Fans
items.excerpt: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC.
items.content_text: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite 's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC. It's been just one week since Epic turned the Item Shop on its head with the launch of its Treasure Hunters mini-season November 1. At the center of the backlash is the Pirate Token, an ultra-rare drop that grants access to the Pirate Shop and effectively makes just about every item in the shop free for 14 days. It's an in-game collectible with unprecedented value, so naturally, it's sent players into a frenzy as they turn over every chest in hopes of finding one for themselves. The problem with a token like this, players have argued, is that they should probably be made aware of the odds of actually finding it so they don't gamble their time on chests that could very likely never yield results. It's transparency that Epic has failed to provide – until now. The developers finally took steps to bring the backlash to an end with a post shared on the Fortnite Service X/Twitter account . Leaving no room for guesswork, Epic spelled out the exact drop rate for this season's treasures and how luck may differ between the average day and Treasure Hours. The one caveat is that Treasure Hours drop rates may be higher in the future, with the team giving the example of a window from tonight that boosts rates for the Pirate Token and Weekly Gold Outfit. You can see the full breakdown below. Fortnite Treasure Hunters Drop Rates Normal Match • 1:1,562,500 - Weekly Gold Outfit • 1:137,500 - Pirate Shop Access • 1:7,813 - Weekly Vehicle & Decal • 1:568 - Weekly Pickaxe or Backbling • 1:391 - Weekly Jam Track • 1:272 - Weekly Loading Screen • 1:127 - Gizmo (any) Treasure Hours • Pirate Shop Access: 1.5x • Weekly Gold Outfit: 7.5x • Weekly Vehicle & Decal: 10x It's the not-knowing that's been most painful for the thousands of fans who have dedicated hours upon hours looking for the Pirate Token in the last week. Some chose to stick to the grind, opening up chests to no avail. Many, many others, however, took their frustrations online . "All Fortnite players deserve equal treatment," one disgruntled player claimed . "Players who barely play get the Pirate Shop Access Token on day one, while longtime players with 3000+ chests get NOTHING. I'm calling on Fortnite players if we don't get this token, let's BOYCOTT FORTNITE FOREVER." Epic responded to claims that not all Fortnite players have an equal opportunity to find rare items like the Pirate Shop Token in an X post . In addition to saying "buying an account or using fake tools is a scam," it confirmed that, like any other chest in Battle Royale, "every player has an equal opportunity to find Pirate Shop Access." @Pirat_Nation Hey @Pirat_Nation - Buying an account or using fake tools is a scam. This is just like any of the chests in Battle Royale, so every player has an equal opportunity to find Pirate Shop Access. — Fortnite Status (@FortniteStatus) November 3, 2026 Hello @FTC, Epic Games added a new "Pirate Token" which doesn't have any public odds of getting it, which creates anti-consumer field/FOMO. The game is majorly played by children, they can do anything if they wouldn't get it, so take action against Epic Games please — KBAHTCET │ QuantSet (@QuantSet) November 5, 2026 You may not be too surprised to see some calling to boycott Fortnite over the confusion surrounding the Pirate Token. What may be a bit more shocking, though, are those who tried to report Epic to the Federal Trade Commission for failing to share odds out of the gate. "What Fortnite has brought upon this game is predatory and is conducting a deceptive business practice making people believe that everyone has a 'FAIR' chance," another player, who said they "wouldn't be surprised" to see the FTC get involved. "I know people as well where entire squads with over 15,000 chests opened and not getting items simply as the car, jam track, pickaxe, or the loading screen. Fortnite needs to have better transparency with the community and their partners when it comes to hosting events like this." We now know that, during most hours of the day, everyone has a 1:137,000 chance of opening a chest that grants Pirate Shop Access. Before the clarification, players had no idea how many chests they should expect to open before letting frustration set in. A few players online had even surmised that the drop rate could be somewhere around 1:7,000, a far cry from what ended up being the reality. @FortniteStatus "1:137,500 - Pirate Shop Access" That's why Luffy still hasn't found the One Piece after 20 years. https://t.co/eSDpRLYZev — UKNON Jones - OUT NOW! (@uknonjones) November 7, 2026 Fans are generally happy to see exact odds on their screens, even if they wish Epic had been more transparent at the season's drop. For now, it's unclear if the studio has any plans to try any moves like this again, or if drop rates will be clarified earlier on. "Thank you, this is what we wanted," @StableRonaldo said . "W Fortnite." "Thank you for transparency but it should not have taken a week," @M1das_OW2 replied . Fortnite again found itself in hot water when players launched a campaign against its Nikki from Obsession skin last month. Epic is reportedly working on a Star Wars and Marvel crossover game, though it was reportedly recently delayed .

items.title: LEGO Black Friday 2026 Sales: What to Expect
items.excerpt: You can expect to see plenty of deals on LEGO sets during Black Friday 2026. I've covered LEGO deals for years, and here's what I expect to see this year.
items.content_text: On nearly every IGN article about LEGO sets (and as the LEGO editor here at IGN, I post a lot of them), commenters complain that LEGO sets cost too much. That’s a fair criticism, especially because many of the most noteworthy LEGO sets are expensive . Even the smaller sets cost more than you might expect if you don’t pay attention to the market. They’re comprised of many tiny interlocking pieces, after all. If you feel like you’re priced out of many LEGO sets you’d want to buy, Black Friday offers an excellent opportunity to buy them at some of the lowest prices of the year. The question is, what kinds of discounts on LEGO can we expect to see this Black Friday? I’ve been covering LEGO deals for many years now, so here’s what I expect based on my experience. LEGO Sets Up to 50% Off Many times throughout the year, LEGO sets go on sale at various retailers. These run-of-the-mill sales generally offer discounts of 20% off. That’s the standard sale price at retailers like Amazon, Target, Best Buy, and the LEGO Store. Therefore, a particularly good sale on LEGO sets is when you can find them for 30%, 40%, or even 50% off . These are the kinds of discounts I expect to see once the true Black Friday sales begin. LEGO Store's Black Friday Sale Unlike many retailers, the official LEGO Store tends to have a pretty short-lived Black Friday sale. Last year's sale started on Black Friday and ran for fours days – which means through that weekend and Cyber Monday. But the LEGO Store won't be the only retailer dropping prices on LEGO sets, so keep an eye on the Black Friday sale schedule to see when retailers like Amazon and Walmart's sales will go live. Discounts on Retiring Sets Which brings us to the question of which sets are most likely to be discounted? Answer: the sets that are retiring soon. LEGO releases hundreds of new sets each year ( here’s our running tally of the 2026 releases ). To make room on retailer shelves for all those new boxes, LEGO has to retires older sets at roughly the same rate. Right now, LEGO’s “retiring soon” page has over 200 sets on it. You can bet many of these will go on sale during Black Friday as retailers try to offload inventory to make way for upcoming LEGO sets . Black Friday LEGO Godzilla Set Each year, LEGO releases a major new set on Black Friday. It’s always a statement piece, and it’s priced accordingly. This year’s Black Friday set is LEGO Godzilla , a towering 5,363-piece set that stands over two feet tall. It features a striking gray-and-blue version of the city-wrecker that looks menacing and highly detailed. I love it. It will be available for $449.99, starting at 12:01 a.m. November 27. If you buy it between November 27 - 30 while supplies last, you’ll also get an additional LEGO set as a free Gift With Purchase. It’s LEGO Godzilla Logo & Footprint , and it’s meant to be displayed next to the King of Monsters. It has matching colors and looks phenomenal. LEGO Insiders Weekend 2026 Every year on the weekend before Black Friday, LEGO runs an “Insiders Weekend” promotion. This is a LEGO Store sale that’s exclusive to LEGO Insiders, a free membership that gets you access to events like this ( you can sign up here ). In addition to discounts on select sets, it also gets you things like bonus loyalty points on purchases, as well as exclusive Gifts with Purchase. You can check out last year’s promotions for an idea of what promotions we might expect to see in 2026.

items.title: Missing Teen Saved From Alleged Kidnapper After Seeking Help in Among Us
items.excerpt: A Utah teenager was rescued from an Oregon man's home after she successfully contacted help from another child in Among Us.
items.content_text: A Utah teenager was rescued from an Oregon man's home after she successfully contacted help from another child in Among Us . Authorities saved the 17-year-old November 1, 2026, after receiving a tip relayed by a younger player she met while playing developer Innersloth's hit party mystery game, according to Newsweek . She had allegedly spent more than 500 days held captive by 39-year-old Adam Harmel after he took her across state lines and prevented her from leaving. The Utah teen was just 15 when she was reported missing in May 2025. Harmel allegedly began contacting her through Snapchat earlier that month before offering to send her money to travel to his home in Oregon. He then made the hours-long drive to her location and lured her into his vehicle, disposing of her phone by throwing it into a river shortly after. Investigators said Harmel forced the teenager to sleep in a bed with him in his basement, becoming increasingly violent through the 521 days she was held captive. She found her window to escape when the alleged kidnapper granted her access to a phone without cellular data. Although unable to contact others via traditional means, the device did allow her to use a WiFi connection to play online games. Among Us, which allows players to communicate and was released for mobile devices in 2018, allowed her to get in touch with another child. After moving the conversation to a different, undisclosed social media app, she then told the other player who she was, revealing that she was actively being held captive at Harmel's home in Oregon. She shared concern that, after more than 500 days of searching, authorities had stopped looking for her. The other child then alerted their mother to the interaction, with the parent then reaching out to the FBI. A subsequent video call with the missing teenager saw her describe her circumstances to investigators. She was rescued from Harmel's property later that day. Harmel has since been arrested and charged with transporting the teenager across state lines with the intent to exploit her.

items.title: Sony Announces Indefinite Delay for PlayStation's Pulse Elevate Wireless Speakers Days Before Launch
items.excerpt: Sony has announced an indefinite delay for PlayStation's Pulse Elevate wireless speakers just days before their global launch.
items.content_text: Sony has announced an indefinite delay for PlayStation's Pulse Elevate wireless speakers just days before their global launch. The tech company announced the last-minute schedule change in a November 6, 2026, update to an existing PlayStation.Blog post . The message cites a recently identified "production issue" that must be attended to, with no new release date shared. "As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," Sony's announcement said. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon." Scroll the tiniest bit further down, and you'll see that Sony had set the Pulse Elevate speakers to launch globally November 12 – just six days out from when the delay update was published. Whatever problem its team encountered must have been pretty significant, but without a new release date or additional information, it's unclear if we'll learn what happened. Sony announced its new PlayStation-branded, $219.99 speakers in September of last year as the latest entry in its collection of Pulse audio accessories, which includes earbuds and headphones. They were said to be available in both Midnight Black and White, with both boasting a built-in microphone with "AI-enhanced noise rejection." The speakers are also able to be paired with PlayStation 5, PC, Mac, and even PlayStation Portal devices. "Pulse Elevate builds upon the immersive next-level gaming audio experience we introduced to players with Pulse Elite wireless headset and Pulse Explore wireless earbuds, combining powerful technologies like planar magnetic drivers and PlayStation Link into new form factors for players to experience with their favorite games," Sony said at the time of the announcement. How many units were manufactured ahead of the delay, or how the new issue may impact these existing speakers, was not made immediately clear. IGN took a closer look at all of the new PlayStation hardware, Pulse Elevate wireless speakers included, back in June. We came away looking forward to how the tech might work in practice, calling its noise rejection system "seriously impressive stuff."

items.title: Mass Effect Cast Celebrates N7 Day With Video Asking Fans to Help Save the Franchise
items.excerpt: Without BioWare, N7 Day is quieter this year, but that didn't stop the Normandy cast and crew from teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect.
items.content_text: Without BioWare, N7 Day is quieter this year, but that didn't stop the Normandy cast and crew from teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect. EA shuttered BioWare , canceled Mass Effect 5 , and put the gaming side of the franchise on an indefinite hold just weeks before the series' annual November 7 holiday, leaving players just as hurt as they were confused. There's not really any official festivities to enjoy this year, but the developers and actors behind the stories and characters fans love still made sure to get together for a special video message. Organized by the unofficial group known as We are Mass Effect, the two-minute video message features appearances from composer Sam Hulick, Jennifer Hale (Commander Shepard/FemShep), Ash Sroka (Tali'Zorah), Keythe Farley (Thane), Kimberly Brooks (Ashley), Mark Meer (Commander Shepard/MaleShep), Steve Blum (Urdnot Grunt), Brandon Keener (Garrus), and many more. One by one, they each call to "Save Mass Effect" in the wake of BioWare's closure, marking what is only the latest shot to garner attention and, hopefully, give the franchise a shot in the arm. Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 7, 2026 "It started feeling like Shepard recruiting the squad in Mass Effect 2!" We are Mass Effect's Mer told IGN when describing the process to make the video. "We were bringing people on board one by one, and Mark was a huge help in making that happen! It almost felt like we were gathering War Assets. And the most surprising thing is that with every video we received, the actors would thank us. "We'd get messages saying, 'Thank you for doing this,' or 'Thank you for your work.' We were the ones who felt incredibly grateful to them for taking the time to participate, but they kept turning around and thanking us. That really touched me. Everyone involved, from the people who made these games to the people who brought their characters to life, cares deeply about this universe." We are Mass Effect and other Mass Effect fans have been busy the last few weeks. After footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect: Universe appeared online just days after EA brought the franchise to a halt, a petition has launched and gained more than 310,000 signatures . A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week. As some have called to boycott EA , others have taken their fight straight to the publisher's front door . We are Mass Effect has been a big part of that initiative, with its first and most notable move arriving when it launched a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square . Yesterday, the group drove a mobile billboard around EA headquarters in Redwood City, California . More billboards are live today, including one posted up around the former BioWare offices in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, with another set to appear around The Game Awards next month. Former project director and executive producer Michael Gamble also sent a message to fans for N7 Day. 🚨 WE ARE IN EDMONTON Today, our mobile billboard is right outside BioWare's former offices. For 30 years, BioWare gave us unforgettable stories and characters. Today, we're standing up for the people who brought them to life. #SaveMassEffect https://t.co/fXa4bemyfE — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 7, 2026 🚨 WE'RE KICKING OFF N7 DAY WITH ANOTHER BILLBOARD This time, #SaveMassEffect has made its way to Cardiff, Wales, thanks to the incredible @psykit. Another amazing initiative from our community, showing that we're not giving up on Mass Effect and BioWare's legacy. https://t.co/4avNpk18jd — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 7, 2026 🚨 WE ARE TAKING OVER TEXAS A member of our community, AngryBaby, has put up #SaveMassEffect billboards in the Frisco and Dallas areas of North Texas. It's incredible to see fans taking the initiative and spreading the movement on their own. HOLD THE LINE 🫡 https://t.co/AoJBppCzbV — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 6, 2026 You all are truly amazing. The love and passion for this…universe…is incredible. Even in worst days, we could always count on you. To all the stories left untold. Happy N7 Day. — Michael Gamble (@GambleMike) November 7, 2026 "We're still holding on to that hope and fighting for the future of Mass Effect, BioWare, and the people who have dedicated so much of themselves to bringing this universe to life," Mer added. "N7 Day is a reminder of what these games mean to all of us, but also of the people behind them. The impact they've had on this community will never been forgotten, and we will continue celebrating it for as long as we can." Meanwhile, as the Mass Effect cast and fans on the ground do their best to celebrate N7 Day, other developers have chimed in to share their love for the series on its saddest holiday so far. Owlcat Games, the team behind the upcoming Mass Effect-inspired RPG The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, shared a video celebrating what BioWare and its work over the decades means to them. "Everybody in Owlcat dreamt about playing Mass Effect 5," studio creative director Alexander Mishulin said. "It's very, very selfish, but we wanted to experience the next chapter in those adventures. Our hearts and minds are with [BioWare], and we really hope they find themselves a new home, different studios that will allow them to make even more worlds, even more experiences, more adventures that we will be amazed at. That will be new beacons for new generations of game developers. This #N7Day is a sad one for all Mass Effect fans. So we want to reminisce about what Mass Effect and many other BioWare games meant to us and how they inspired us. https://t.co/HKG5XkLA28 — Owlcat Games (@OwlcatGames) November 7, 2026 "It will be not Mass Effect, but it will be something else, and something beautiful." BioWare's final years were captured on video and will soon be shared in a new documentary . For more, you can check out IGN's interview with one modder who has rebuilt Mass Effect 3's multiplayer . You can also read about how AI is impacting the modding scene .

items.title: BioWare May Be Dead, But a Modder Has Rebuilt Mass Effect 3's Multiplayer Into the Legendary Edition
items.excerpt: When the Mass Effect Legendary Edition came out in 2021, it included the single player campaign of all three original games, along with all the DLC. But while all the story content you could ever want was included, Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode was conspicuously absent, despite having a dedicated fanbase.
items.content_text: When the Mass Effect Legendary Edition came out in 2021, it included the single player campaign of all three original games, along with all the DLC. But while all the story content you could ever want was included, Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode was conspicuously absent, despite having a dedicated fanbase. Now, just a few weeks after EA's shutdown of BioWare , a team of modders has successfully ported Mass Effect 3 's multiplayer to the Legendary Edition, with all the graphics and engine improvements that came with that re-release. The mod will be coming out on N7 Day – November 7th – and will be free to play, as long as you already own Mass Effect Legendary Edition. I also got a chance to sit down with Mgamerz, who runs the ME3Tweaks team that created the mod, to talk about Mass Effect 3, and about the state of modding in 2026. And if you want to download the mod yourself, it's available now on Nexus Mods. IGN: So, tell me a little bit about the project, and how you got started on basically porting the Mass Effect 3 multiplayer over to the Legendary Edition. Mgamerz: Yeah, so my dev team, ME3Tweaks, and I run it. We ported Pinnacle Station back in 2021. Crazy effort. I don't know how we got that done in a two-month timeframe. And then we were doing other projects for two years, and then near the end of me working on LE2 Randomizer, which is a randomizer for legendary Mass Effect 2, someone discovered a copy of the Citadel in Mass Effect 2. There's an area from the wards. I can't remember which game it was, but they found an area of the game that nobody knew about before, and you could load into and you're like, 'Well, this was clearly supposed to be something, and then they just never finished it.' It was a very early prototype. And it was like, 'Man, what if we could port something like that into another level?' And so I made this project called Project Wardle, Ward being the first part of it. (We have a bunch of stupid internal code names.) And I eventually made it so we could port a Mass Effect 2 level into Mass Effect 3, and we fixed up the cover, because cover is just an unbelievable nightmare. It's very important for enemies to be able to use it. Gameplay's a huge component of why Mass Effect 3 is fun. And we got that working and then I was like, 'Well, man, what if we could port the multiplayer levels?' Because we did it for Pinnacle Station. We ported the old game. But Pinnacle Station is mostly just reused assets from Mass Effect 1. Like 90% of it was just existing assets that they just reused. But multiplayer was totally different. It's like, yeah, none of this content exists. So the scope of work is just huge. So at the end of 2023, right as we finished LE2 Randomizer, literally on N7 day, I spun up a new Discord. I invited a couple people and they're like, 'What's this Discord about?' I'm like, 'We're going to do something stupid. We're going to port [Mass Effect 3] Multiplayer.' And those were the first two messages I ever sent. I have some screenshots of it. And then people were like, 'Yeah, you're joking, right?' And I'm like, 'No.' And then the last three years we've been working on it. It hasn't been constant. Last year I broke my arm, which set us back six to eight months. But for the first two years, it was tons of prototyping. Within the first month of this project, we actually had multiplayer working. It was a proof of concept. And then we spent the next two years getting audio to port, from a different version of the audio engine because they upgraded it. It's like we got shaders building, which was a total nightmare because BioWare compiled the game with a bunch of sources that don't ship with the game. And so we had to figure out 'how do we replicate that?' So that took a long time. And then it's like textures. We have a bunch more people that know how to do texture upscaling. The first two years is almost all prototype and then asset generation. We want to make it look good. We're planning stuff out, that kind of stuff. So that's really not how it started. IGN: So, you basically built from scratch again? Did you take assets from the original Mass Effect 3? Mgamerz: Oh yeah, the whole thing ports from it. It's not a one-to-one port. We're not just taking Mass Effect 3 multiplayer and dumping it into Legendary Edition and then, 'Hey guys, check out it's multiplayer, [as] you remember it.' Where we took a lot of extra steps, the lighting actually gets re-baked in Unreal Engine 4's light solver. Essentially what that means is, imagine you have a light bulb in a room and if you wanted to project what the lights would look like, a light beam's going to hit your microphone and it's going to cast a shadow. And then that light bounces off for you, goes into your closet and it bounces off and illuminates the closet a little bit from the inside. Unreal Engine 3 had a solver and that's how all of the lighting for all the Unreal Engine 3 games worked. But in Unreal Engine 4, they added like, 'Oh, we can do additional light bounces or we found a better statistical way to do light bounces.' And so you get crisper shadow edges or the more soft, like a grate covering on some maps. The light bounces through the grate, and unless you have super high resolution textures, it looks terrible. Mass Effect 3 is full of terrible light maps. If you look at them, you're like, 'Wow, it's just a big stair step of shadows and it looks bad.' And so we spent a lot of time upgrading that kind of stuff. I modded Mass Effect 3 multiplayer for eight years before Legendary Edition came out, and there's a bunch of stuff I was like, 'Wow, I didn't even realize three of the character classes don't even use the highest-quality mesh.' So it's like BioWare made the Geth Infiltrator, and they made it at a high quality where it has all the polygons and triangles. And then as you get further away from the camera, it gets less triangles, because you can't see as much detail. But BioWare was just like, 'We're just not going to use the highest quality one. We'll ship it in the game, but you'll never see it.' And so it's like, 'Oh, well, we can just turn those on and it's an immediate quality upgrade.' IGN: Was quality a big reason why you took on this massive undertaking to bring ME3 multiplayer to Legendary Edition? Because if I understand correctly, the servers for the original ME3 multiplayer are still working, for now at least. Mgamerz: By the time we publish this, I don't know, man. N7HQ's gone, so I wouldn't be surprised if it disappears before. Actually, the whole reason this project started, I was getting to the end of LE2 Randomizer and I was like, 'Man, I love Mass Effect 3 multiplayer.' I modded tons of stuff into it, and it was really fun. I went back and I was like, 'I want to make a new one. I want to make a new mod.' I went back to it and I was like, 'These tools,' and I'm totally throwing myself under the bus, 'These tools suck. There's no debug tools. Everything is so immature compared to what we have in Legendary Edition, thanks to what BioWare changed for us.' And so I was like, 'Man, I'd rather just port multiplayer than have to deal with this awful development environment.' And then I was like, 'Okay, well, I've modeled this forever.' I know where all of the pain points are in extending this because I made a new map pack, I made a new enemy pack that adds a new faction. So I'm like, 'I know where all the landmines were, because I had to pioneer it.' And I'm like, 'What if we rebuilt multiplayer and accounted for those landmines so if someone else wants to do it, they don't have to go through the same landmines, or they're at least aware that they're there?' So there's a bunch of considerations for extensibility. As a user, if you just go in and you just play Standard, you might not notice the changes, but the next dev who wants to add a new faction, it'll be like, 'Wow, I don't have to deal with all these stupid problems that I would've had in the original game.' And so a lot of stuff like that that people won't appreciate, but will make a difference in the long run. IGN: And it'll probably mean more mods end up coming out for it, as well. So, I'm sure you had a certain amount of people that you expected to play this once you launched it. How much did BioWare's closure change your expectations for your launch date? Mgamerz: We were already targeting N7 Day. It was probably about in early August, late July. We were getting to a point where it was like, okay, this is fully playable. It doesn't crash. The shaders look right. It's like, this is something we could probably ship by N7 Day. I was more like, We should probably ship this in January. But then I was like, it's N7 Day . I hate doing the N7 Day crunch, but I always do it, because I secretly feel like I'm a masochist and I kind of enjoy it. There's a satisfaction of essentially killing yourself to get the thing out the door and then being like, oh, it's finally done. I am a hundred percent ready as of this interview to ship this thing. There's so much stress going on around this release that's killing me. But Bioware's closure, honestly, didn't really factor into it [the release date] at all. IGN: Do you think you're going to get more people checking it out though? Mgamerz: Oh yeah, because there's tons of attention on Mass Effect right now, so I'm sure there's going to be a lot more, which is adding to the stress. I've done launches like this for years, and I know on the first day, stuff's going to be broken. I mean, I've been developing software, the mod manager and stuff, and you launch a new feature and some user clicks a button you didn't think they'd click at the exact frame of the installer or whatever, and the whole thing dies. So I'm expecting the first day to just be kind of a train wreck, which sucks, but it's just how it is. It'll get better over time. IGN: Do you expect that EA is going to pull access to some of the tools that are necessary for modding the game? Mgamerz: I don't think so. We had an NDA with BioWare back in 2021. It's expired by now, but they had my dev team, not the current dev team — there's a couple more members now, but more core members back then — they had us all under NDA before Legendary Edition launched, and we provided some input to help modding. So they clearly were interested in having modders to some degree as part of it. I don't know if new EA ownership shares that same view, so it's a little concerning, but I mean, our game requires you own Mass Effect Legendary Edition. This was never going to be like DotA where, "Hey, we split the game off and you get to go do whatever." The goal has always been, "You own Mass Effect Legendary Edition. We're going to source assets from it during the install." Our game is technically self-contained, so it's not like a mod into Mass Effect 3. It generates a new copy of essentially Mass Effect 3, we call it LMP, and it's fully standalone. So all of your existing mods, they actually don't work with the new install by design because we don't want people immediately installing and immediately breaking everything. It's one of those landmines that working on the old stuff, I know for a fact doing that will break multiplayer for a lot of people. So I'd rather be more restrictive at launch and then relax it as we figure it out versus, "Hey guys, here's all this stuff. You install a bunch of mods and then it just doesn't work on day one." And you're like, "Well, I'm never going to come back to this again." IGN: Yeah. Are you hoping to support this project long term, then? Mgamerz: Yes. Yes. Multiplayer is my jam, dude. I racked up thousands of hours, probably at least a thousand hours in the first year before Origin even tracked how long you played the game. And then I have another 2,800 hours on top of that, and most of it was modding multiplayer. And then I don't even know how much I have in Legendary Edition. I don't really play Legendary Edition. I never really played the original games, either. It was just always multiplayer. Everyone that's ever interviewed me is like, "You must love the story." And I'm like, "I've played the trilogy, the actual trilogy played through maybe twice since 2012." IGN: So if you weren't really into the story of Mass Effect, how did you get into the multiplayer? Mgamerz: Oh, well, I played Mass Effect 1 shortly before Mass Effect 3 came out because [of] the ads. It was actually on GameSpot. It was just littered with ads. You couldn't do anything on the page without there being a Mass Effect 3 ad. And I was like, "Oh, that looks kind of cool." And so I played Mass Effect 1. I used some texture mods and made it look better. I'm like, "Oh, this is kind of a nice game. I'm enjoying this." And then Mass Effect 2 was pretty good. Then I got to Mass Effect 3, played about halfway through it, and then I was like, "Ah, maybe I'll try multiplayer." And then it was fun. I had a good time. And this is where my modding career on this game started. I was playing, it was on Firebase White, and every enemy was a husk, and there were 30 of them, and my poor laptop was dying. There were 30, but my computer was like, "Kill me, just end me right now." I remember asking on voice chat in the game, I was like, "Is anyone else's game freaking out? Why is it all husks?" And some other person was like, "I don't know, man, it must be some sort of glitch." And I was like, "Huh, weird glitch." And obviously now I know that the person was modding the game, but I had so much fun. I was like, "Man, how do I do that?" And then I learned how to do it and made my little mod manager, and then I just kept getting more and more ambitious until here we are porting multiplayer. IGN: How did you get your start in modding? Was it with Mass Effect 1? Those texture mods? Mgamerz: No. My technical first part of modding was SimCity 4 when I made the world's worst 3D model of a library. I think it's still on Simtropolis. I won't tell you my original username, but it was essentially just a donut and a block underneath it, and everyone roasted me for it because it was so trash. I was like 13 or something. I was super young. I didn't know what I was doing. But then my real modding started. I got into GameMaker, which is a game development app. It was really great for learning how to program without having to learn how to program. It taught you concepts like a random chance is a dice roll. That's something everyone could understand. So it was a visual language, and I made a couple of small games. They were really fun. I really enjoyed it. And then I found a decompiler for something called Ninja Fight Screensaver, and it's just two boxes with little limbs attached. It's just a physics simulation and it just moves them back and forth. And then the physics will cause the arm to swing, and they would calculate damage based on the velocity, and there'd be some stupid blood particle effects. It looked terrible, but I was like, "Man, I'd love to make my own level in this game." So I found a decompiler for a GameMaker build, decompiled the game, and found tons of unused levels and stuff. I was like, "Whoa, this is awesome. There's a truck in this," which was never in the released version of the game, but it's like, "Oh my God, they made a truck." I was like, "That's awesome." And then I actually got into Mega Man Battle Network modding back in the old days. I remember doing online net battles before the Legacy Collection, before CapCom re-released it. And I was like, "Man, I remember doing that back in the day playing other players like 2006 or something." And that was all assembly modding. You have to learn how to read pretty much machine code. Really difficult, but really fun. Very dedicated little community. I took a break from modding for a couple of years, and then Mass Effect 3. IGN: How do you feel about the pervasiveness of cloud-based AI decompilation ports and the mashup mods? Mgamerz: Boy, it's a mix. So for the first two years of this project, we didn't even use AI at all. If you could use it, which I never did, it probably wasn't up to par to get any of the stuff done that we would really need it to do. There's been some mods recently released in this scene, and I'm not going to mention any names. I'm not targeting any specific ones. In the modding community, you have an ecosystem. For example, I have my mod manager, you deploy mods through the mod manager, it runs a bunch of checks on the mods to make sure you're not going to ship something that's just going to break someone's game immediately. And there's certain knowledge, like you don't put stuff in startup files because it wastes tons of memory. If you stuff everything in there, you boot the game, oh, now the game takes an extra gigabyte of memory for your single mod to work because you didn't want to do it the proper way. So there's an ecosystem of knowledge that when you start modding, you have to integrate yourself into so you can play nice with everyone's stuff. Is it as convenient as typing a prompt into Claude, "Hey, make me this mod?" Of course not. For our AI usage, and in relation to your question, there's a difference between what I call vibe coding, where you just kind of prompt it until you get what you want, and having expertise in understanding what it's actually writing and you're reviewing it, that's more like AI assisted. For decompilation specifically, we've used Claude for some of it, but a majority of our decomp was already done before AI tools were even available. I can tell you from just seeing what it can do, it's insane how good it is. The problem is when you make it so... This will sound like gatekeeping, and it kind of is. I'm just being honest with you, it's kind of gatekeeping. The difficulty of making mods and getting into it filtered out a lot of low-quality stuff. You see this on stuff like the Switch eShop. It's full of slop, because there's no quality control, and you can just ship whatever, and then users have to dredge through all sorts of stuff like that. There's a balance. I want to make my tools easy for people to use. I don’t want it to be like, you have to be the most masochistic person to get into modding, but I also don't want it to be like you type a prompt into Claude and you can just ship something that doesn't have any awareness of [whether] it's going to break everything else. We've seen mods where the description and the images of the mod are not even human-written. The directions are straight up wrong. The images don't even show the content.
